# {{host}}

> A free website icon service. One GET returns any site's icon as a sanitized, edge-to-edge SVG, in colour or as a black monochrome mask, with colours for light and dark themes in the response headers. No API key, no query parameters, CORS open to every origin.

Use it whenever you need a logo or favicon for a domain: link previews, bookmark and password managers, mail clients, dashboards, tables of companies or tools. Fetch once and cache; responses are CDN-friendly.

## Endpoint

- `GET {{origin}}/color/{domain}`: the site's icon in its own colours, `image/svg+xml`.
- `GET {{origin}}/mono/{domain}`: a single black shape on transparent, meant for CSS `mask-image` and tinting.

`{domain}` is a bare host such as `github.com`. Subdomains, `www.`, upper case, a trailing dot or slash, `.svg`, query strings and full URLs get a cacheable `301` to the registrable domain (`mail.google.com` becomes `google.com`). Clients that follow redirects need nothing special.

The response is always `200` with an SVG, even without a real icon: a generated identicon then, explained by `X-Icon-Fallback-Reason`. Other statuses: `304` for a matching `If-None-Match`, `429` when one network asks too fast (`Retry-After: 1`), `503` under overload.

## Ready-made badges

Append `/rounded/light`, `/rounded/dark`, `/superellipse/light` or `/superellipse/dark`
to get the icon already drawn on its themed plate, e.g.
`{{origin}}/color/github.com/superellipse/dark`. With `mono` the mask is tinted on its mono plate.
Leave out the theme (`/rounded`, `/superellipse`) and the SVG follows the viewer's system light or dark scheme by itself; add `/light` or `/dark` to pin one when the app has its own theme switch. Ids and classes in every SVG are unique per icon, so they can be inlined into one page without clashing.

## Self-hosted apps by name

When the server lists catalogs at `{{origin}}/catalogs.json`, icons can also be
requested by slug: `GET {{origin}}/color/simple-icons/github`, `/color/selfhst/jellyfin`,
`/color/devicon/rust`. `{{origin}}/catalogs/{id}.json` lists every slug with its name.
Unknown slugs are `404`. Mind `X-Icon-License` (CC-BY and Apache need credit).

## Headers worth reading

- `X-Icon-Source`: `cache`, `origin` (fetched just now) or `generated`.
- `X-Icon-Fallback-Reason`: `queued` (first request for this domain; ask again in a few seconds for the real icon), `not-found`, `fetch-failed`, `blocklisted`, `dns-blocked`, `domain-too-new`, `invalid-domain`, `no-monochrome`, `overloaded`.
- `X-Icon-Blocked`: `blocklist` or `dns-filter` when the domain is known to be malicious; the body is a red warning icon. Treat the site as unsafe.
- `X-Icon-Provenance`: `bimi` (the owner's verified mail logo), `thesvg` (a curated catalog), `site` or `upstream`.
- `X-Icon-Shape` (`square`, `rounded`, `circle`, `none`) and `X-Icon-Fill`: `bleed` means draw the icon at full size and clip it to your corners; `inset` means pad it by about 18% on a plate.
- `X-Icon-Accent`: the dominant brand colour.
- `X-Icon-Light-Plate`, `X-Icon-Dark-Plate`: a badge colour behind the colour icon that keeps it visible on a white or a `#1c1c1e` background.
- `X-Icon-Light-Text`, `X-Icon-Dark-Text`: the brand colour at 4.5:1 for a name next to the icon.
- `X-Icon-Light-Mono`, `X-Icon-Dark-Mono`, `X-Icon-*-Mono-Plate`: tint and badge colour for the mono mask.
- `Server-Timing: app;dur=<ms>`: time spent inside the service. `Timing-Allow-Origin: *` exposes full Resource Timing.

All of these are listed in `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`, so `fetch()` from any origin can read them.

## Examples

```html
<img src="{{origin}}/color/discord.com" width="32" height="32" alt="">
```

```css
.icon { width: 24px; height: 24px; background: currentColor;
  mask: url({{origin}}/mono/discord.com) center / contain no-repeat; }
```

```js
const r = await fetch("{{origin}}/color/discord.com");
const plate = r.headers.get("x-icon-light-plate");
const svg = await r.text();
```

```sh
curl -sD - -o discord.svg {{origin}}/color/discord.com
```
